annotation.reasoning_summary: Polygon features map housing-corporation-owned building/block areas and their attributes; this is not a full tessellation or reporting-unit layer. The decisive rule is ObjectDS for identifiable bounded real-world property objects, with numeric fields treated as attributes rather than the main phenomenon.
Point features represent archaeological finds/cesspit locations as distinct mapped objects, not measurements or events.
Point features mark selectable archaeological find spots/locations with address, research, and finds; this is an object layer, not a measurement or event layer.

Polygon features are individual archaeological sites/vindplaatsen, each a distinct mapped place/object with address and excavation details. Not a full tessellation; object-based polygons fit the object rule.

Polygons mark barbecue restriction/permission areas in parks and plantsoenen, so they are selected policy/affected zones rather than a full tessellation or mapped objects; PatchDS is the decisive rule.
Polygons mark protected conservation areas and cultural-historical zones, not a full tessellation or reporting units; entity is a bounded policy/heritage area patch.
Point features mark survey/inventory observations of wild bees by place and year; the main phenomenon is the occurrence of inventory observations over time, so PointDS + EventDS.
Point locations are mapped, and the layer’s main message is the numeric number of honey bee hives/colonies at each location (amount is the mapped phenomenon).

The layer maps soil-quality zones that apply across areas and together form a near-complete zoned partition, so geometry is a tessellation. The main phenomenon is a bounded policy/condition area (soil quality zone), not discrete objects or reporting units, so entity is PatchDS.
Point features represent individual trees (mapped objects) with species, planting year, and other attributes; numeric fields are identifiers/attributes, not the main phenomenon.
Point layer of individual trees; each point represents a distinct mapped object (tree), not a measurement or event. Numeric fields are attributes of the trees, not the main phenomenon.
Point geometry with 70k tree locations; each point represents a distinct tree object (species, year, owner/manager attributes), not a measurement or event.
Point geometries map individual trees as countable real-world objects; numeric fields like plant year and radius are attributes, not the main phenomenon.
Point features mark distinct compost initiatives at specific addresses/places; the layer maps real-world objects, not measurements or events.

Polygons form a near-complete area layer of camera/overlast areas, so geometry is a tessellation. The named gebieden are selected zones where a condition applies, matching PatchDS rather than reporting units or objects.

Point layer of individual trees; each point represents a distinct real-world object (a specific Canadian poplar), with attributes like species and planned measures. The decisive rule is point-object mapping, not the numeric boomnummer or management fields.
Point geometries marking distinct counted sensors/cameras; the map is about identifiable monitoring objects, not measurements, events, or amounts.

Polygon areas are selected culture-historical exploration zones and protected areas, not a full tessellation or reporting units. The map represents bounded phenomenon/applicability areas, so PatchDS is the best fit.
Point layer of mapped knotweed occurrences/observations; the points are the features themselves, not measurements or events, so ObjectDS best fits.
Point features map discrete ecopassage/barrier sites and crossings, so the layer is mainly a set of identifiable objects rather than measurements or events.

Polygons are selected potential wind-energy areas, not a full tessellation or reporting units; the decisive rule is PatchDS for bounded zones where a phenomenon/policy applies. The layer maps potential areas and their power/yield attributes, so geometry is PlainVectorRegion.
Point layer of vote locations; the main mapped phenomenon is numeric election results shown by circle size and percentages, so this is PointDS + AmountDS.

Point layer of oak processionary caterpillar nests with real-time mutations and status changes over time; the decisive rule is EventDS for something that occurs/changes, not a static object or amount.
Polygons mark pedicab allowed/forbidden areas, so this is a selected restriction/policy zone layer rather than a tessellation or object layer; PatchDS fits the area-of-applicability rule.
Point features marking pedicab and carriage stand locations; the mapped thing is a distinct place/object (standplaats), not a measurement or event.

Point features are individual BAG addresses/verblijfsobjecten, and the layer maps non-residential function categories for each address/object rather than a measurement or event. ObjectDS fits the mapped real-world objects; the numeric fields are attributes, not the main phenomenon.
Polygons form near-complete block-street partitioning, and the layer is a full-area categorical function-mix classification (wonen/voorzieningen/werken), so CoverageDS with tessellation geometry.
Neighborhood polygons form a near-complete administrative/reporting partition (buurten/wijken/stadsdelen), so geometry is VectorTessellation and entity is LatticeDS.
Neighborhood/borough area layer with polygons that partition Amsterdam into reporting units; reporting-unit rule gives LatticeDS and the polygon set is a tessellation.
Neighborhood polygons form an administrative/reporting-unit tessellation (buurten/wijken/stadsdelen) with codes and area attributes, so the layer is a lattice of statistical units.
Neighborhood/buurt polygons form a reporting-unit tessellation of Amsterdam; this is a classic lattice of administrative/statistical areas, not an object or patch layer.
City districts are administrative/reporting units that partition Amsterdam into polygons, so the geometry is a tessellation and the entity is LatticeDS.
Administrative reporting units (stadsdelen/wijken/gebieden/buurten) forming a near-complete partition; classify as tessellation and reporting-unit lattice rather than object or patch.
Administrative area layer of buurten/wijken/gebieden/stadsdelen; polygons form a reporting-unit tessellation, so geometry is VectorTessellation and entity is LatticeDS.

The layer maps Amsterdam areas such as buurten, wijken, gebieden, and stadsdelen, which are reporting/administrative units forming a near-complete partition, so Geometry is VectorTessellation and Entity is LatticeDS.
The layer shows named Amsterdam buurten/wijken/gebieden/stadsdelen, which are reporting/administrative units forming a near-complete area partition, so VectorTessellation with LatticeDS.

Administrative area layer of Amsterdam neighborhoods/districts/areas; polygons form a near-complete partition, so Geometry is VectorTessellation. The features are reporting units (buurten, wijken, stadsdelen) with area attributes, so Entity is LatticeDS.
Polygon regions represent industrial noise contour/zone areas with dB thresholds, so this is a bounded phenomenon patch rather than a reporting unit or object.
Polygon isoline/band layer for noise levels (55-60, 60-65, etc. dB), so the decisive rule is contour/value-band mapping rather than object or patch.
Polygon contour bands of noise levels (50-55, 55-60, etc.) indicate isolines/value intervals, so this is a contour layer rather than objects or reporting units.
Polygons are noise contour zones with dB classes (50-55, 55-60, etc.); this matches contour/interval bands rather than objects or a tessellation.
Point geometry with voting-station locations; the main mapped phenomenon is numeric election results per stemlocatie, so this is a point amount layer rather than simple objects or measures.
Point geometry with addresses and named rooftop sites indicates distinct real-world objects/places (green roofs), not measurements or events.
Land use 2017 is a full-area thematic land-use classification over many polygon units, so the geometry is a tessellation and the entity is CoverageDS.
Point geometries map distinct historical buildings/archeological sites with names, functions, and dates; this is a point object layer, not a measurement or event layer.

The layer maps three named Amsterdam boundary polygons that are meant to be moved/rotated for area comparison; they are discrete municipal/regional objects, not a tessellation or patch. Geometry is PlainVectorRegion and the decisive entity rule is ObjectDS.
Polygon areas marking dog leash, off-leash, prohibition, and seasonal restriction zones; they are selected applicable areas rather than a full tessellation or reporting units, so PatchDS.

Polygon areas represent selected green-structure zones and restrictions/policy areas, not a full tessellation. The layer is about bounded green areas where green functions and planning rules apply, so PatchDS fits better than ObjectDS.
Point geometry and the layer maps individual trees (distinct, countable objects) with attributes like species and planting year; numeric fields are object attributes, not the main phenomenon.
Point geometry with each feature representing a discrete housing project/building complex; numeric dwelling counts are attributes, not the main mapped phenomenon, so ObjectDS rather than AmountDS.
Point geometry with 5,159 individual chestnut trees as mapped features, each with species and damage status attributes. The decisive rule is point objects, not amounts or events.
Point geometries are sampling locations with numeric groundwater/soil-related values (Maaiveld, GLG, GLG_maaiveld); the layer is a point measurement map, not objects or areas.
Polygon areas show flood-risk zones tied to probability/depth classes, not reporting units or full tessellation; this is a bounded phenomenon/affected-area map, so PatchDS.
Point dataset of fixed market locations; each point represents a distinct market/place, not a measurement or event. ObjectDS fits the mapped feature, with time/day fields as attributes only.
Point geometry and the layer maps distinct named green monuments/bijzonder bomen as objects; the numeric monument number is just an attribute, so ObjectDS.
Point features map individual monumental trees, which are distinct real-world objects; numeric fields are attributes, not the main phenomenon.

Point geometry and the layer maps monuments as identifiable real-world objects/facilities; decisive rule is ObjectDS for discrete monuments, not AmountDS because the numeric monument ID is not the mapped phenomenon.

Point layer of actual plant growing locations; each point represents a distinct occurrence/object, not a measurement or event. Numeric fields are counts of specimens, but the mapped feature is the plant location itself.
Point measurements of NO2 concentration at monitoring stations/buoys; the layer represents sampled air-quality values at locations, so PointDS + PointMeasuresDS.
Point layer of NO2 measurement locations; the map is about measured concentrations sampled at stations/buisjes, so PointDS with PointMeasuresDS.

Polygons mark the Oergeul as a selected geologic influence/constraint zone around the IJ, not a reporting unit or full coverage; this fits PatchDS. The polygons do not appear to tessellate the area, so geometry is PlainVectorRegion.
Point dataset of boreholes/soundings used to measure subsurface properties; the main phenomenon is sampled measurements at locations, so PointDS + PointMeasuresDS.

Polygon regions are named development neighbourhoods (ontwikkelbuurten) with codes and stadsdeel labels, so the layer is a tessellation of bounded reporting areas; the mapped features are the neighbourhood objects themselves rather than a coverage or patch zone.
Point geometry; each feature is a distinct public toilet facility/amenity, so the decisive rule is ObjectDS for mapped objects.

Polygons are neighbourhood/area units named by Buurtnaam, so this is a tessellated reporting-unit layer. The policy text is attached to the units, but the decisive rule is reporting units -> LatticeDS.
Polygon areas form a near-partitioned gebiedsindeling for parking standards; the map shows policy/applicability zones for new construction, so VectorTessellation + PatchDS.
Polygon layer of named parks/green spaces; these are discrete bounded places rather than a full tessellation or reporting units, so ObjectDS with PlainVectorRegion.

Polygon postcode areas are reporting/statistical units (postcode4/buurten), so LatticeDS. They are discrete postcode polygons, not a full tessellation of land use or coverage map in the strict sense; geometry is PlainVectorRegion.
Polygon postcode4 areas are reporting/statistical units, and the map is explicitly about postcode zones following buurt boundaries; this fits LatticeDS on a tessellated polygon layer.

Polygon postcode areas form a near-complete partition, so Geometry is VectorTessellation. The mapped features are postcode6 reporting units derived from address buffers and grouped by postcode, so the decisive entity rule is reporting unit -> LatticeDS.
LineString features map Amsterdam plus- and main transport networks; the layer is about connected infrastructure/route priority, so NetworkDS with LineDS.

Polygons depict Amsterdam pedestrian plus/net areas tied to a traffic policy framework, so the main phenomenon is a bounded policy/priority zone rather than reporting units or objects. The regions do not form a full tessellation, so PlainVectorRegion; entity follows the patch rule.
Point geometries with named locations and privacy statements; the mapped features are distinct sites/facilities, so ObjectDS rather than amount or event.

Point geometry with markers for privacy-related investigations/risk analyses and camera/sensor privacy notices; the mapped features are occurrences/activities tied to specific locations, so EventDS fits best.
Point layer of camera/sensor locations with addresses and privacy statements; each point is a distinct mapped object/place, not a measurement, event, or network.
Point layer of election polling/stemlocatie sites where circle size encodes vote counts and percentages; the mapped phenomenon is numeric election amount, not the places themselves.
Polygon areas mark Rainproof drainage/problem zones where overlast applies, not a full tessellation or reporting units; this fits the patch/phenomenon-area rule.

Polygons represent Rainproof hydro problem/solution areas tied to extreme-neerslag overlast, not discrete objects or reporting units. The set is a near-complete partition of Amsterdam hydro units, so VectorTessellation with PatchDS fits the selected phenomenon zones/areas.
Polygons mark discrete rainproof bottleneck/overlast zones from a simulation, not a full tessellation or reporting units. The layer is about affected areas where the phenomenon applies, so PatchDS.
Polygon areas mark Rainproof nuisance/overlast locations from a 3Di simulation, i.e. selected phenomenon zones rather than a tessellation or discrete objects; this fits PatchDS.
Point features represent individual religious buildings/locations (addresses, building names, genootschap), so this is PointDS with ObjectDS rather than amount or event.
Line geometries map sidewalk segments, and the main phenomenon is sidewalk width/comfort as a numeric magnitude, not a network of routes.
Line geometries and the layer maps a traffic regulation/route system for mopeds on the roadway; decisive rule is NetworkDS for connected transport/roadway lines.
Point geometries, and the layer maps public sports facilities/playgrounds as distinct named amenities; numeric oppervlak is just an attribute, so ObjectDS.
Point locations represent individual city farming sites/initiatives (locations, names, addresses); this is a point object layer, not measurements or events.
Polygons represent discrete city farming locations/parks/tuinen with names and addresses, so ObjectDS; they are separate bounded places, not a full tessellation or patch zone.
Point layer of 678 records; each point marks where space-seekers were established over the past 9 years, so the main phenomenon is occurrences/events rather than objects or measurements.
LineString features named 'Major streets' indicate a connected street system, so this is a network layer rather than objects or amounts.

The layer represents district heating/cooling transport lines, i.e. a connected utility network. Geometry is LineDS because all features are LineString transport lines; entity is NetworkDS because the main phenomenon is the transport system, not the line objects individually.

The layer maps district heating/cooling network areas, not reporting units or objects; the metadata explicitly says transport lines were simplified and wijk lines buffered into polygons, so the main phenomenon is a connected utility network (NetworkDS) with polygon buffers rather than a tessellation.

Polygons represent named housing development projects/plan areas, not a full tessellation. The decisive rule is ObjectDS for discrete projects/facilities; numeric woning counts are attributes, not the main mapped phenomenon.
Point features with names, addresses, products, and opening times indicate distinct food initiative locations/farms; this is a point object layer, not measurements or events.
LineString features and the description explicitly say this is the tram/metro network of stations, stops and lines; route system takes priority, so LineDS + NetworkDS.
LineString features and metadata explicitly describe the tram/metro network of lines, stations, and stops; this is a connected transport system, so NetworkDS with LineDS geometry.
Point features represent tram stops and metro stations, and the layer is explicitly the tram/metro network of stations, stops, and lines; network is the decisive entity rule.
Point features represent tram stops and metro stations, and the layer is explicitly about the tram/metro network rather than simple objects or amounts.
Point features represent individual traffic-light-regulated intersections with names, IDs, status, and dates; this is an identifiable object layer, not a measurement or event layer.

Line geometries represent road links, and the main mapped phenomenon is traffic volume/prognosis values on those links (etmaal and time-period counts), so this is a line-based amount layer rather than a network-only route map.
Point locations are voting stations, but the main mapped phenomenon is numeric election results displayed by circle size/amounts at each location, so PointDS + AmountDS.
Point features represent individual trees as discrete real-world objects; the numeric fields are attributes (species, planting year, size classes), not the main mapped phenomenon.

Point geometry with individual traffic information system objects (cameras, displays, pollers) described as distinct assets; classified as ObjectDS, not AmountDS, because the numeric fields are identifiers/attributes.
Point features mark distinct traffic information system objects (installations/equipment) shown on the map; the layer is an object inventory, not a measure or event.
Point features mark distinct bird nesting/breeding locations at addresses/buildings; the layer is about mapped nesting places, not point measurements or events.
Point geometry with each feature representing a distinct Vondelpark bench; adoption status is an attribute, so the decisive rule is ObjectDS for countable mapped objects.
LineString street segments are the mapped features, and the layer is about sidewalk walkability along the street network with policy input values, so LineDS + NetworkDS.
Point features represent individual wall art works at specific building locations; this is a set of identifiable objects, not measurements or events.

Polygon areas form a near-complete citywide thematic partition of welstand levels, so geometry is VectorTessellation. The layer maps regulatory/quality zones and applicable policy areas rather than discrete objects, so entity is PatchDS.
Polygons form a citywide partition into welstand areas/systems, so VectorTessellation. The layer maps planning/regulatory style areas where welstand policy applies, not discrete objects, so PatchDS.
Point geometries mark WWII attack incidents/impacts at locations with dates and descriptions; the decisive rule is EventDS for something that happened over time, not an object or measurement layer.

Polygon project areas are mapped, but the layer’s main message is housing plan quantities ('De aantallen vormen de planvoorraad'); numeric totals are the phenomenon, so AmountDS. The polygons are discrete project areas rather than a tessellation.
Point features map self-build plot projects/available building sites; the layer is about discrete real-world project objects, not a measurement or network. Points imply PointDS.

Polygon footprints are individual buildings/daksituaties, but the layer’s main meaning is the applicability/possibility of solar panels under heritage rules, so PatchDS. Polygons do not form a tessellation, so PlainVectorRegion.
Point geometries map detected solar panel systems, and the main phenomenon is numeric magnitude (count and estimated capacity/vermogen) rather than point objects alone, so PointDS + AmountDS.

Point features represent named swimming and play-water locations/facilities; this is a point object layer, not a measure or event. The decisive rule is point geometry with distinct real-world places, so ObjectDS.
